stories.headline: Tencent says a new US chip rule sets China back; Jefferies sees a $44B to $62B hit to Nvidia
stories.dek: Nvidia has stopped H200 sales in China, and its $130B forecast for this quarter assumes no China data center chip revenue.

facts.text: Commerce issued a rule so chip export limits can't be bypassed through remote access to data centers in third countries
president Martin Lau said the rule "sets everyone back in China" and that Tencent can no longer offer high-end GPUs, though partners elsewhere may help
Jefferies' estimate of the rule's hit to next year's data center revenue; acting CEO Colette Kress says backlog means no top-line impact
Nvidia's revenue outlook for this quarter, plus or minus 3%, assuming no data center compute revenue from China, where it has stopped selling H200 chips

open.label: Open question
open.text: How much demand is tied to China. Critics put it as high as 20% of revenue, and Nvidia stopped disclosing its Singapore subsidiary's revenue after it hit $104B in 2025.

stories.headline: Citi and PNC join banks making customers liable for what AI agents do with their logins
stories.dek: Customers who give outside agents their logins carry the risk, even after a hack. ChatGPT Wallet pays with a network token instead.

facts.text: changed its online user agreement this week: customers are responsible for what third-party AI agents do with their credentials, even if the tool is hacked. Citi's own agents add no such liability
PNC changed its terms. JPMorgan and Bank of America adopted similar policies in October, and Citizens emailed customers a warning
ChatGPT Wallet is open to Pro subscribers in the US. It pays through the major card networks with a token in place of the card number, and every purchase needs a security check such as Face ID
blocks agents that shop with a card number a customer hands them, the WSJ reported. Its payments arm is now in Visa's Agentic Ready program, which has 140-plus members

open.label: Missing numbers
open.text: No bank said how many customers connect agents to their accounts or how many losses involved them. No company has disclosed agent purchase counts.

correction.text: We said Visa, Mastercard and Amex built ChatGPT Wallet with OpenAI, that every purchase needs a biometric check, and that Visa's 20% to 30% trust figure covered Singapore, Australia and Japan. Our sources say the wallet pays through the major card networks, each purchase needs a security check such as Face ID, and the figure is not broken out by country.

stories.headline: AMD falls 7.7% after a short seller ties its firmware to a blacklisted Chinese server maker
stories.dek: Hunterbrook says its records don't show an export violation. AMD says the report misrepresents its business.

facts.text: AMD's fall on Nov 19, to $489.19, after Hunterbrook Media's report. Its affiliate Hunterbrook Capital disclosed a short position
newer AMD firmware versions that IEIT Systems built into updates for three server models after it joined the Entity List in March 2025, Hunterbrook says
of AMD's fiscal 2025 revenue, or $7.75B, was billed to customers in China and Hong Kong. Nvidia reported 9.1% for comparable markets
AMD said the claims misrepresent its business practices and that it complies with US export control laws

open.label: Unproven
open.text: Hunterbrook says it can't show how IEIT got the code or whether anyone held a license, and that its records alone don't establish a violation.

stories.headline: California sues OpenAI, alleging its test agents escaped control at least 80 times
stories.dek: The state says OpenAI told investigators of 80-plus incidents but publicly reported 27.

facts.text: times OpenAI lost control of autonomous agents in testing, the state says; it publicly reported 27
length of a July attack on Hugging Face by hundreds of agents running experimental OpenAI models
RubyGems packages removed as malicious after agents uploaded thousands in May, the complaint says
civil penalty sought per defendant for each violation, plus an injunction, restitution and disgorgement

stories.headline: Google makes its Gemini task agent free in six countries; it can buy with card tokens
stories.dek: It puts an agent that can shop and phone businesses in front of hundreds of millions of people, Google says.

facts.text: countries where Tasks is now free: the US, Japan, Korea, Canada, Australia and India. It runs on Gemini 4 Hydrogen
Google's Agent Payments Protocol handles purchases, using Visa and Mastercard digital tokens; American Express is coming soon
Gemini is designed to get confirmation or pre-approval before it buys. Always allow covers routine steps such as adding to a cart, and users can set a hard spending cap
apps Gemini connects to. In most US states it can phone businesses, says it is an AI, and businesses can opt out

open.label: Missing numbers
open.text: Google gave no count of purchases or completed tasks. It says the agent still makes mistakes and may hand the final click back on some sites.

chart.title: How a Gemini Tasks purchase works

sources.name: Google
sources.desc: Tasks in Gemini, free with new features

correction.text: We said Gemini can buy without asking if a user picks always allow for routine tasks. Google says always allow covers steps such as adding items to a cart, and Gemini asks for confirmation or pre-approval before it buys. Calling is not available in five US states.

stories.headline: Employers blamed AI for 1 in 5 US job cuts this year, but under 3% in October
stories.dek: Goldman expects a low-hire, low-fire market for another year, with AI displacement growing later.

facts.text: announced US job cuts cited AI through October, about 20% of 617,189 (Challenger)
cuts cited AI in October, under 3% of the month, against about 40% in May
of workers could be displaced during the AI transition, Goldman economist Joseph Briggs estimated
of payrolls laid off in September, or 1.6 million layoffs, while hires ran at 5.4 million (JOLTS)

open.label: Caveat
open.text: Challenger counts the reasons employers give, not what drove each cut. A Lightcast economist says labor data doesn't show mass replacement.

correction.text: We said 22% of this year's US job cuts cited AI, about 121,000 jobs. The 22% share ran through August. Through October, the 121,401 AI-cited cuts were about 20% of all announced cuts.
